ledger.note: 1010: the Banu Qasim make Alpuente a taifa. 'It was ruled by a Berber family of the Banu Qasim tribe'; the taifa 'existed from around 1009 to 1106', 'created following the end of the Caliphate of Córdoba ... in 1010'. The page gives the city, not a boundary; the region is Cliopatria's 1010 shape plus the capital's district.

1106: the Almoravids take Alpuente. 'Conquered by the Almoravids: 1106' (infobox); (rulers table: 'Abd Allah II 1043-c. 1106). The Alpuente town page says 'In 1103, Alpuente fell under the Almoravid dynasty'; the Almoravid page has Valencia occupied in 1102 and the Albarracín page has it conquered in 1104.
1106: the Taifa of Alpuente ends; the land passes to the Almoravids (see the loss event). Cliopatria draws a shape to 1110.

notes: Taifa of Alpuente 1010-1106. Page budget 5; seven pages opened but none of them has a territorial event for Alpuente beyond its end, so the ledger is three events. UNSETTLED: (1) End 1106 (taifa article, infobox) against 1103 (Alpuente town page) against Cliopatria's 1110; 1106 is kept. (2) Start: the article says 'from around 1009' and 'created ... in 1010'; Cliopatria's 1010 is kept. (3) Cliopatria's shape (all five rows share the same bbox) does not contain the town of Alpuente; a 25 km district is added in every correction and in the found and dissolve regions. (4) Vassalage to Valencia, Toledo or Zaragoza and the border with Albarracín (Cliopatria neighbours 1015-1110) are not on any page opened; the Valencia page is silent on Alpuente. (5) The small shape changes of 1066 and 1085 (about 100 km2) are not explained by any page and are left without events. (6) The town page also says Alpuente passed 'to the emirate of Murcia in 1229' and, in the next sentence, was 'conquered by the king of Aragon in 1229'; after 1106 it is outside the state's life. Gazetteer names used that it lacks: Alpuente (place).
